purpose: decide which service business to start in California (cleaning, landscaping, sign hanging, towing or baking), register and license it correctly, equip it, and win and keep service contracts from retailers, property managers, municipalities and residents across Turlock and the wider state
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors grounded in how California small service businesses are registered, licensed, insured and contracted
the founder starts small with limited capital and may begin solo before hiring, and wants recurring contract income rather than a single job
specific fee thresholds, permit names and tax rules are reasoned and must be confirmed against current CA Secretary of State, CSLB, CDTFA, local health and CHP/DMV rules before relying on them
exclusions: general wage employment (delegated to the Turlock wage-jobs KB)
commercial driving credentials and the driving-instructor license (delegated to the paid-driving-credentials KB), except the tow-carrier permits a towing business needs
tax preparation and legal counsel beyond pointing at the registrations, licenses and insurance a service business needs

competency_questions.question: Which service business fits the founder's skills, capital and capacity?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BIZ_IDEA_FIT matches a service to capacity and STARTUP_CAPITAL sizes the money needed to begin

competency_questions.question: Who buys these services and what kinds of contracts exist?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MARKET_DEMAND_SCAN names the buyers and CONTRACT_TYPES classifies one-time, recurring, seasonal and on-call agreements

competency_questions.question: What business entity should be formed and how is it registered?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BIZ_STRUCTURE picks an entity on liability and tax and REGISTER_AND_TAX lists the state, local and tax registrations

competency_questions.question: What trade-specific licenses and permits does the chosen service require?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LICENSES_PERMITS maps each trade to its license or permit (contractor, food, tow, applicator)

competency_questions.question: What insurance and bonding are required to operate and to sign contracts?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: INSURANCE_BONDING lists liability, commercial auto, workers' comp and bonds and why clients demand certificates

competency_questions.question: What equipment and vehicle does each trade need to deliver?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: EQUIPMENT_BY_TRADE lists the gear per trade and VEHICLE_AND_HAULING covers the truck, trailer or tow rig

competency_questions.question: Where are supplies sourced and how is labor added legally?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SUPPLIES_AND_SUPPLIERS names wholesale sourcing and CREW_AND_LABOR covers contractor-vs-employee classification

competency_questions.question: Where does a new contractor find service contracts?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FINDING_OPPORTUNITIES lists facility managers, brokers, public bids and residential channels

competency_questions.question: How do large retailers like Walmart actually contract cleaning and maintenance?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RETAIL_FACILITIES_PATH explains contracting through national facilities-management vendors and how to register as a subcontractor

competency_questions.question: How does a towing business get contracts?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TOWING_CONTRACTS covers motor-club networks, police rotation lists and property/fleet impound and how to qualify

competency_questions.question: How should the contractor bid, price and register as a vendor?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BIDDING_AND_PRICING prices to fully-loaded cost plus margin and VENDOR_REGISTRATION covers onboarding, COIs and certifications

competency_questions.question: How are contracts delivered, kept and paid?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CONTRACT_MGMT_QUALITY covers SLAs and renewals and CASHFLOW_INVOICING covers invoicing and net-term cashflow

competency_questions.question: How does the business scale safely and what is the startup roadmap?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SCALE_AND_RISK weighs growth against overextension, STARTUP_ROADMAP sequences the launch and REVIEW_LOOP sets renewals

glossary.definition: a limited liability company, a common entity for service contractors that separates personal assets from business liability and is filed with the California Secretary of State
a 'doing business as' or fictitious business name, filed with the county so a business can operate and bank under a trade name

a Contractors State License Board license, required in California for construction-related work, including larger landscaping and structural sign work, above a dollar threshold of combined labor and materials
a CDTFA permit required to sell tangible goods such as baked products, used to collect and remit sales tax
a limited home-based food business permitted under California's Homemade Food Act to make certain low-risk foods up to an annual sales cap without a commercial kitchen
a COI, the document a contractor gives a client to prove it carries the required liability, auto and workers'-compensation coverage
a national company that holds the master maintenance contract for a retail chain and subcontracts the actual cleaning and repair to local providers
the DMV permit a commercial hauler, including a tow operator, must hold to operate, alongside CHP tow regulations and any police rotation requirements
the California AB5 standard that presumes a worker is an employee unless they meet all three conditions to be an independent contractor, governing how crew is classified

source_registry.description: heuristic prior estimates for starting a California service contracting business, reasoned from CA Secretary of State entity registration, local business licensing, CSLB contractor licensing, CDTFA seller's permits, county health permits and cottage-food rules, CHP/DMV tow-carrier requirements, and standard facilities-management subcontracting and bidding practice
source_registry.citation_or_locator: method modeled on CA Secretary of State LLC/corporation filing, city business license and DBA filing, IRS EIN, CSLB contractor license thresholds, CDTFA seller's permit, county environmental health food permits and the California Homemade Food Act, DMV motor carrier permit and CHP tow regulations, and the AB5 ABC worker-classification test; no proprietary dataset supplied

nodes.definition: Match a candidate service to what the founder can actually deliver: cleaning and landscaping need low capital and quick start, sign hanging needs ladders or a lift and sometimes a license, towing needs a costly truck and permits, and baking needs a permitted kitchen, so the idea is chosen against skills, capital, vehicle and crew.

included: matching a service to skills, capital and capacity

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the founder's capital, skills or local saturation changes

pros.claim: Choosing a service the founder can resource avoids launching one that capital or skills cannot support
pros.example: starting with janitorial, which needs little capital, before a tow business that needs a truck

cons.claim: The lowest-barrier service may be the most competitive and lowest-margin
cons.example: residential cleaning being crowded and price-pressured

failure_modes: choosing a high-capital trade with no money to equip it
picking a service the founder cannot physically or legally deliver
acceptance_tests: the chosen service is matched to the founder's skills, capital, vehicle and crew
revisit_triggers: the founder's capital or capacity changes
a chosen trade proves oversaturated locally

nodes.definition: Scan who buys the service and where demand sits across Turlock and California: retailers and chains, property and facility managers, HOAs and apartment complexes, municipalities and schools, fleets and dealerships, other businesses, and residents, distinguishing steady business-to-business buyers from one-off residential ones.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: buyer demand or the business's credibility changes

pros.claim: Knowing the buyer types aims the business at steady commercial demand rather than thin one-off work
pros.example: targeting property managers for recurring janitorial over scattered house cleans

cons.claim: Commercial buyers are harder to land and demand insurance and references a new business lacks
cons.example: a facility manager requiring three references the startup cannot give

failure_modes: building for residential one-offs when recurring commercial pays steadier
ignoring a strong local buyer segment
acceptance_tests: the main buyer segments are listed and ranked by steadiness and reachability
revisit_triggers: a buyer segment grows or dries up
the business gains the references to reach commercial buyers

nodes.definition: Estimate the capital and runway to launch: equipment, vehicle, licenses, insurance deposits, supplies and working capital to cover the gap before the first invoice is paid, so the founder begins only with enough to reach paying contracts and does not stall mid-launch.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: startup costs or time-to-payment change

pros.claim: Sizing capital and runway prevents launching a business that runs out of money before its first paid contract
pros.example: budgeting for insurance and supplies plus weeks of runway before net-30 pays

cons.claim: Over-conservative capital planning can delay a launch that modest funds could start
cons.example: waiting to save for a full crew when a solo start was viable

failure_modes: launching with no runway for the net-payment gap
underestimating insurance and license costs
acceptance_tests: the estimate covers equipment, licenses, insurance, supplies and runway to the first paid invoice
revisit_triggers: equipment or insurance prices change
the expected time to first payment changes

nodes.definition: Choose the business entity on liability and tax: a sole proprietorship is simplest but exposes personal assets, an LLC adds a liability shield commonly used by service contractors, and a corporation suits larger operations, balancing protection against filing cost and complexity.

included: sole prop vs LLC vs corporation

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the business's size or liability exposure changes

pros.claim: An LLC shields personal assets from business claims that service work can create
pros.example: a liability claim from a slip on a cleaned floor hitting the business, not the home

cons.claim: An LLC adds formation cost and an annual state fee a bare sole proprietorship avoids
cons.example: paying the annual franchise tax even in a slow first year

failure_modes: operating as a sole proprietor in a high-liability trade with no shield
forming a complex entity a tiny business does not need
acceptance_tests: the entity choice is justified by the trade's liability and the founder's tax situation
revisit_triggers: the business grows or adds employees
liability exposure rises

nodes.definition: Complete the registrations that make the business legal to bill: file the entity with the California Secretary of State if an LLC or corporation, file a fictitious-business-name DBA with the county, get a federal EIN, obtain a city business license and tax certificate, and register a CDTFA seller's permit if selling goods such as baked products.

included: state, county, city and tax registrations

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: registration requirements or the business location change

pros.claim: Completing registrations lets the business bank, invoice and contract under its name legally
pros.example: opening a business account with the EIN and DBA to accept contract payments

cons.claim: The web of state, county and city filings is easy to leave incomplete
cons.example: forgetting the city business-tax certificate and facing a penalty

failure_modes: operating without a required city business license
missing the seller's permit when selling taxable goods
acceptance_tests: entity, DBA, EIN, city license and any seller's permit are all filed
revisit_triggers: the business moves city or adds a taxable product line
a registration nears renewal

nodes.definition: Obtain the trade-specific licenses and permits the chosen service legally requires: a CSLB contractor license for construction-grade landscaping or structural sign work above the dollar threshold, county health permits and a cottage-food or commercial-kitchen path for baking, DMV and CHP tow-carrier permits for towing, and an applicator permit if applying chemicals.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: trade licensing rules or the work scope change

pros.claim: Holding the right trade license lets the business take regulated, higher-value work legally
pros.example: a CSLB license enabling larger landscaping contracts a handyman cannot legally take

cons.claim: Licensing adds exams, fees and time before regulated work can begin
cons.example: the months and bond a CSLB license requires

failure_modes: doing licensed-scope work without the license and facing penalties
exceeding cottage-food limits without a commercial kitchen permit
acceptance_tests: each regulated activity the business will perform is matched to the license or permit it requires
revisit_triggers: the business takes on larger or newly regulated work
a licensing threshold or rule changes

nodes.definition: Carry the insurance and bonds needed to operate and to sign contracts: general liability, commercial auto, workers' compensation once there are employees, garage-keepers cover for towing, janitorial bonds, and surety bonds, since nearly every commercial client requires a certificate of insurance before work begins.

included: liability, auto, workers' comp and bonds

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: client insurance requirements or the business's exposure change

pros.claim: Holding the required coverage both protects the business and unlocks contracts that demand a COI
pros.example: providing a liability certificate that lets a property manager sign

cons.claim: Premiums, especially workers' comp and commercial auto, are a heavy fixed cost early on
cons.example: commercial auto for a tow truck costing a large monthly sum

failure_modes: bidding work the business cannot insure to the client's requirement
skipping workers' comp once employees are hired
acceptance_tests: the business carries the coverage its trade and clients require and can issue a COI
revisit_triggers: a client raises its insurance requirement
the business adds employees or vehicles

nodes.definition: Acquire the equipment each trade needs to deliver to a commercial standard: cleaning uses commercial vacuums, floor and carpet machines and chemicals; landscaping uses mowers, trimmers, blowers and a trailer; sign hanging uses ladders or a lift, drills and anchors; towing uses a wheel-lift or flatbed truck, dollies and straps; baking uses commercial ovens, mixers and packaging.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: contract requirements or equipment condition change

pros.claim: Matching equipment to the trade lets the business meet a commercial quality and pace standard
pros.example: a commercial floor machine making a retail janitorial contract feasible

cons.claim: Buying top-grade equipment upfront can sink scarce capital before revenue
cons.example: buying a new tow truck before any contract exists

failure_modes: under-equipping so commercial quality cannot be met
over-investing in equipment before contracts justify it
acceptance_tests: the equipment list meets the target contract's quality and volume at an affordable cost
revisit_triggers: a contract demands capability the current gear lacks
equipment fails or needs replacement

nodes.definition: Provide the right vehicle and hauling capacity: a van or truck and trailer for cleaning and landscaping crews, a stake or box truck for sign work, and a wheel-lift or flatbed tow truck with the DMV motor-carrier permit and CHP compliance for towing, sized to the routes and loads the contracts demand.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: route, load or tow-permit requirements change

pros.claim: The right vehicle lets crews and loads reach the job and meet response-time terms
pros.example: a flatbed tow truck meeting a motor club's response and load requirements

cons.claim: Specialized vehicles, especially tow trucks, are a major capital and insurance burden
cons.example: the cost and commercial-auto premium of a tow truck before steady contracts

failure_modes: a vehicle too small for the route or load
operating a tow truck without the motor-carrier permit
acceptance_tests: the vehicle meets the contract's load, route and response requirements and is permitted
revisit_triggers: routes or load sizes grow
tow regulations or permit rules change

nodes.definition: Source consumables and parts at wholesale to protect margin: cleaning chemicals and paper from janitorial and restaurant-supply distributors, landscaping fuel and parts, sign anchors and hardware, and baking ingredients and packaging from warehouse and business-supply sources, buying in bulk and tracking cost per job.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: supply prices or volume change

pros.claim: Wholesale sourcing keeps the per-job consumable cost low and the bid margin intact
pros.example: buying cleaning chemicals by the case rather than retail bottles

cons.claim: Bulk buying ties up cash and storage before the work that consumes it
cons.example: a pallet of supplies sitting unused while contracts are still pending

failure_modes: paying retail for supplies and eroding margin
running out of a critical supply mid-contract
acceptance_tests: consumables are sourced wholesale with a known cost per job
revisit_triggers: supply prices change
contract volume changes the supply need

nodes.definition: Add labor legally as the business grows: start solo, then hire help classified correctly under California's AB5 ABC test, where most crew must be employees with payroll and workers' compensation rather than independent contractors, weighing the cost of employees against the misclassification risk.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the crew size or classification rules change

pros.claim: Correct classification avoids the back-pay, penalties and liability of treating employees as contractors
pros.example: putting a regular crew on payroll instead of paying cash as 1099

cons.claim: Employees bring payroll tax, workers' comp and management overhead that thin early margins
cons.example: workers' comp premium on a small crew cutting into job profit

failure_modes: misclassifying employees as contractors under AB5
scaling labor before contracts can pay for it
acceptance_tests: each worker is classified correctly with required payroll and workers' comp in place
revisit_triggers: the business adds regular workers
classification rules change

nodes.definition: Classify the contract forms the business can win: one-time jobs, recurring janitorial or maintenance agreements, seasonal landscaping contracts, on-call towing rotations, supply or service agreements, and subcontracting under a larger vendor, choosing forms that give steady, predictable revenue.

included: one-time, recurring, seasonal, on-call and subcontract forms

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: contract economics or available forms change

pros.claim: Targeting recurring agreements builds predictable revenue instead of constant rebidding
pros.example: a monthly janitorial contract versus chasing one-off cleans

cons.claim: Recurring contracts can lock in a rate that inflation or rising costs erode
cons.example: a multi-year contract whose fixed rate falls behind wage costs

failure_modes: chasing one-off jobs when recurring revenue was available
locking a long fixed rate without an escalation clause
acceptance_tests: the target contract forms are chosen for revenue steadiness and risk
revisit_triggers: costs rise against a fixed-rate contract
a steadier contract form becomes available

nodes.definition: Find contract opportunities through the channels that fill them: direct outreach to property and facility managers, national service brokers and facilities-management vendors that subcontract chain work, government bid portals such as Cal eProcurement and county and city RFPs, trade networks, and online and neighborhood channels for residential work.

included: direct outreach, brokers, public bids and online channels

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a contract-finding channel's yield changes

pros.claim: Working facility managers and bid portals reaches contracts that never appear on consumer sites
pros.example: responding to a county RFP for grounds maintenance

cons.claim: Public bids and broker onboarding are slow and paperwork-heavy for a new business
cons.example: a government bid requiring certifications the startup lacks

failure_modes: waiting for inbound leads instead of direct outreach
ignoring public bid portals that list steady contracts
acceptance_tests: at least two contract-finding channels are actively worked
revisit_triggers: a channel stops producing leads
the business qualifies for a new channel such as public bids

nodes.definition: Understand how large retailers such as Walmart actually contract cleaning and maintenance: they rarely sign store-by-store with a local cleaner but instead hold national contracts with facilities-management companies that subcontract the work, so the path in is registering as an approved vendor or subcontractor in those companies' portals and meeting their insurance and pricing terms.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a chain's facilities-vendor or terms change

pros.claim: Registering with facilities-management vendors opens steady chain work without selling each store individually
pros.example: becoming a subcontractor that services several retail locations on one agreement

cons.claim: National vendors often pay low per-site rates and impose strict terms and slow payment
cons.example: a per-store cleaning rate that barely clears cost after travel

failure_modes: cold-calling individual stores that have no authority to contract
accepting a national rate that does not cover cost
acceptance_tests: the retail path is pursued through the correct facilities-management vendor portal with terms understood
revisit_triggers: a chain changes its facilities vendor
vendor terms or rates change

nodes.definition: Win towing contracts through the trade's specific channels: motor-club and roadside-assistance networks such as auto clubs and app platforms, police and municipal rotation tow lists with their equipment and response requirements, and direct impound and roadside agreements with dealerships, fleets, apartments and property managers.

included: motor clubs, police rotation and property/fleet impound

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: tow-network requirements or rates change

pros.claim: Joining motor-club networks and rotation lists provides a steady stream of dispatched tows
pros.example: qualifying for an auto-club network that dispatches roadside calls

cons.claim: Rotation lists and clubs impose strict response times, equipment standards and sometimes low set rates
cons.example: a police rotation requiring fast response and specific truck classes

failure_modes: pursuing tow contracts before holding the carrier permits and insurance
accepting club rates that do not cover truck and fuel cost
acceptance_tests: tow contract sources are matched to the permits, equipment and response the business can meet
revisit_triggers: a network changes its rates or requirements
the business adds a qualifying truck

nodes.definition: Bid and price to win profitable work, not just any work: walk and measure the scope, price from fully-loaded cost (labor, supplies, equipment wear, insurance, travel and overhead) plus a margin, use per-square-foot or per-service rates where standard, and submit a clear proposal that does not underbid below cost.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: costs, competition or scope change the right price

pros.claim: Pricing from fully-loaded cost protects the business from winning contracts that lose money
pros.example: including insurance and travel in a per-visit rate rather than just labor

cons.claim: Disciplined pricing can lose bids to competitors who underprice, sometimes unsustainably
cons.example: losing a bid to a rival who omitted overhead and later failed

failure_modes: underbidding below cost to win and losing money over the term
omitting overhead or travel from the bid
acceptance_tests: every bid is priced above fully-loaded cost with a stated margin
revisit_triggers: costs rise against existing bids
a pattern of lost or unprofitable bids appears

nodes.definition: Complete the vendor onboarding that lets a client actually pay the business: submit a W-9, certificates of insurance, references and any safety documents, register in the client's or broker's vendor portal, and obtain small-business, minority or disadvantaged-business certifications that open public and corporate set-aside contracts.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: vendor onboarding or certification requirements change

pros.claim: Being a fully onboarded, certified vendor unlocks contracts closed to unregistered providers
pros.example: a small-business certification qualifying the firm for set-aside public work

cons.claim: Onboarding and certification paperwork is slow and must be kept current
cons.example: a lapsed insurance certificate suspending an active vendor account

failure_modes: winning a bid but stalling on incomplete vendor onboarding
letting a COI or certification lapse and losing vendor status
acceptance_tests: the business is registered as a vendor with current COIs and any certifications it qualifies for
revisit_triggers: a certification or COI nears expiry
a new client requires additional onboarding

nodes.definition: Deliver and keep contracts by meeting the agreed standard: hit the service-level terms, run quality checks, communicate proactively, fix issues fast, and earn renewals, because the first weeks of reliable delivery decide whether a contract renews and refers more work.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: service quality or a renewal status changes

pros.claim: Reliable delivery turns a first contract into renewals and referrals, the cheapest growth there is
pros.example: a property manager renewing and referring a peer after flawless service

cons.claim: Over-servicing beyond the contract erodes the margin the bid was built on
cons.example: doing unbilled extras that consume the job's profit

failure_modes: losing a contract to early quality slips
over-delivering free work and erasing margin
acceptance_tests: the contract's service-level terms are met and tracked with a renewal in view
revisit_triggers: a quality complaint arises
a renewal date approaches

nodes.definition: Manage invoicing and cashflow so the business survives the gap between doing work and being paid: invoice promptly, set and enforce payment terms, expect net-30 or net-60 from commercial clients, take deposits where possible, and fund the gap with reserves or financing so payroll and supplies are covered.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: payment terms or the cash reserve change

pros.claim: Managing the cashflow gap keeps the business solvent while waiting on net-term payment
pros.example: holding reserves to cover payroll while a net-60 invoice is outstanding

cons.claim: Financing the gap with credit adds interest cost that eats margin
cons.example: factoring invoices at a fee to bridge a payment gap

failure_modes: taking a large contract without funding its net-term gap
slow invoicing that delays already-late payment
acceptance_tests: the cashflow gap for each contract is funded before the work is committed
revisit_triggers: a client extends payment terms
the contract pipeline outgrows the cash reserve

nodes.definition: Scale deliberately while filtering bad growth: add crews, routes, trucks or contracts only when cash and quality can support them, and reject the dead-end contracts, lowball national-vendor rates and overextension that sink small service firms chasing volume without margin.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: capacity strain or a growth offer changes the calculus

pros.claim: Pacing growth to cash and quality avoids the overextension that kills profitable small firms
pros.example: declining a fourth contract until the third is staffed and paid

cons.claim: Caution can cede a growth window to a faster competitor
cons.example: passing a cluster of contracts a rival then locks up

failure_modes: taking on more contracts than cash and crew can deliver
growing on lowball rates that add work without profit
acceptance_tests: each growth step is added only when cash, crew and quality can support it
revisit_triggers: a contract strains capacity
a low-margin growth offer appears

nodes.definition: Synthesize a dated launch roadmap: chosen service, then registration, license, insurance, equipment and vendor onboarding in order, then first-contract acquisition, each step with a cost and a date and funded from prior progress, so the founder has one affordable, time-ordered path from idea to first paid contract.

included: sequenced launch milestones, dates and costs

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a milestone or an early opportunity changes the sequence

pros.claim: A dated, funded roadmap turns scattered startup tasks into one executable launch
pros.example: registration and insurance by week three, first bid by week six

cons.claim: A rigid roadmap can ignore an early contract that should reorder the steps
cons.example: delaying a ready buyer to follow the written sequence

failure_modes: a roadmap with no dates that never launches
sequencing a costly step before income supports it
acceptance_tests: the roadmap has dated, costed milestones from registration to first paid contract with a fallback
revisit_triggers: a milestone is hit or missed
an early contract opportunity reorders the plan

nodes.definition: Keep the business compliant and current: renew the business license, trade licenses, insurance certificates and certifications on their cycles, refresh pricing against rising costs, and reassess the service mix and contract pipeline when regulations, demand or capacity change.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a renewal date or a material cost/regulation/demand change occurs

pros.claim: Tracking renewals keeps licenses, insurance and vendor status from lapsing and halting work
pros.example: renewing the COI before it expires to stay an active vendor

cons.claim: Constant reassessment can churn a plan that should be executed steadily
cons.example: re-pricing every contract monthly and unsettling clients

failure_modes: a lapsed license or insurance suspending operations
letting fixed prices fall behind rising costs
acceptance_tests: renewal dates and a reassessment trigger list are tracked and acted on
revisit_triggers: a license or insurance renewal nears
costs, regulations or demand shift materially

edges.why_related: the chosen service determines what capital the launch needs
the target buyer scale informs the runway and capital required
the trade's liability profile informs the entity choice
the chosen entity sets which registrations are filed
the service decides which trade licenses and permits apply
trade licensing typically follows basic registration
the entity and its exposure shape the coverage needed
some licenses and bonds are prerequisites to the required insurance
the service dictates the equipment list
available capital bounds what equipment can be bought
the equipment determines the vehicle and hauling capacity needed
the equipment in use defines which consumables to source
payroll and classification require the business to be registered first
hiring employees requires workers' compensation coverage in place
the buyers identified shape which contract forms are available
the target contract form guides where to look for it
the retail-chain path is one specific opportunity channel
towing contracts are a trade-specific opportunity channel
tow contracts require the carrier permits to be in hand
the contract form determines how it is bid and priced
cost structure and overhead feed the fully-loaded price
vendor onboarding requires certificates of insurance
onboarding is done for the specific client or portal found
the won bid defines the standard that must then be delivered
the contract's price and terms set the invoicing and cashflow plan
growth is paced by the ability to keep delivering quality
cash position gates how fast the business can scale
the roadmap sequences insurance as a launch milestone
equipment acquisition is a dated step in the roadmap
first-bid readiness is a roadmap milestone
vendor onboarding is sequenced into the launch plan
renewals and review follow the roadmap's milestones
winning a contract can pressure pricing below a profitable rate
edges.resolution_rule: never bid below fully-loaded cost to win; walk away from a contract that cannot be priced to margin

edges.why_related: hiring to grow competes with staying solo to conserve capital
edges.resolution_rule: stay solo or minimal until contracts reliably fund correctly-classified labor, then hire

edges.why_related: fast growth competes with maintaining service quality on current contracts
edges.resolution_rule: protect existing-contract quality first; add new work only when current delivery is solid and staffed

edges.why_related: national-vendor rates can fall below a profitable price
edges.resolution_rule: accept national-vendor subcontracts only when the per-site rate clears fully-loaded cost with margin

edges.why_related: reassessment feeds renewed demand insight back into the search
cost changes found in review feed back into pricing

conflict_axes.name: win_contract_vs_profitable_price
conflict_axes.description: landing a contract competes with pricing it to actually make money
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: never bid below fully-loaded cost; a lost low-margin bid is better than a money-losing win

conflict_axes.name: solo_low_cost_vs_crew_scale
conflict_axes.description: staying solo keeps costs low while hiring is needed to grow but adds payroll and AB5 risk
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: scale labor only when contracts reliably fund correctly-classified employees

conflict_axes.name: recurring_b2b_vs_onetime_b2c
conflict_axes.description: steady recurring commercial work competes with higher-touch one-off residential jobs
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: favor recurring commercial for predictable revenue once references allow

conflict_axes.name: national_vendor_vs_direct_client
conflict_axes.description: subcontracting under a national vendor is steady but low-rate, direct clients pay more but are harder to win
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use national-vendor work only when net-positive; build direct clients for margin

conflict_axes.name: grow_fast_vs_keep_quality
conflict_axes.description: adding contracts quickly competes with delivering quality on current ones
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: grow only when current delivery is solid and funded

conflict_axes.name: low_capital_trade_vs_high_capital_trade
conflict_axes.description: cleaning and landscaping start cheap while towing and baking need heavy equipment and permits
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: match the trade to available capital; start low-capital and reinvest toward high-capital trades

conflict_axes.name: cottage_food_vs_commercial_kitchen
conflict_axes.description: a low-cost cottage-food bakery is capped in scale while a commercial kitchen costs more but scales
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: start cottage-food to test demand, then move to a permitted kitchen to scale

conflict_axes.name: cash_now_vs_net_terms
conflict_axes.description: the business needs cash now but commercial contracts pay on net-30 or net-60 terms
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: fund the gap with reserves or deposits before taking net-term contracts

conflict_axes.name: licensed_scope_vs_unlicensed_risk
conflict_axes.description: staying under license thresholds limits work while licensed scope opens bigger but regulated jobs
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: license before taking regulated-scope work; never perform licensed work unlicensed

edge_cases.description: landscaping job exceeds the CSLB license threshold
edge_cases.trigger: a contract's labor-plus-materials crosses the contractor-license dollar limit
edge_cases.mitigation: obtain the CSLB license or keep jobs under the threshold

edge_cases.trigger: sales or product type pass the Homemade Food Act limits
edge_cases.mitigation: move to a health-permitted commercial kitchen before exceeding the cap

edge_cases.trigger: operating a tow truck before the DMV motor-carrier permit and CHP compliance
edge_cases.mitigation: secure the motor-carrier permit and tow compliance before any paid tow

edge_cases.description: national janitorial vendor pays below cost
edge_cases.trigger: a facilities-management subcontract rate does not cover fully-loaded cost
edge_cases.mitigation: decline or renegotiate the rate; do not take loss-making volume

edge_cases.description: client requires coverage the business lacks
edge_cases.trigger: a contract demands a COI or workers' comp not yet held
edge_cases.mitigation: obtain the required coverage before signing

edge_cases.trigger: regular workers are paid as 1099 contractors
edge_cases.mitigation: reclassify as employees with payroll and workers' comp

edge_cases.description: net-60 payment opens a cashflow gap
edge_cases.trigger: payroll and supplies are due before the invoice is paid
edge_cases.mitigation: fund the gap with reserves, deposits or financing before committing

edge_cases.description: an underbid contract loses money over its term
edge_cases.trigger: a fixed-rate contract priced below true cost
edge_cases.mitigation: re-price at renewal and avoid underbidding to win

edge_cases.description: equipment breakdown halts service with no backup
edge_cases.trigger: a mower, machine or tow truck fails mid-contract
edge_cases.mitigation: keep a backup or rental plan for critical equipment

edge_cases.description: public bid requires certifications not held
edge_cases.trigger: an RFP requires a small-business or disadvantaged-business certification
edge_cases.mitigation: obtain the certification before bidding set-aside contracts

edge_cases.description: sign or board hanging needs structural or electrical permits
edge_cases.trigger: a sign job involves structural mounting or electrical work
edge_cases.mitigation: obtain permits or partner with a licensed contractor for that scope

workflow.action: pick the service that fits capacity
workflow.description: match a service to skills, capital and capacity
workflow.gate: the service is matched to the founder's resources

workflow.description: identify who buys and what contracts exist
workflow.gate: buyer segments and target contract forms are identified

workflow.description: form the entity and file all registrations
workflow.gate: entity, DBA, EIN, city license and any seller's permit are filed

workflow.description: get the license or permit each regulated activity needs
workflow.gate: every regulated activity is matched to its license or permit

workflow.description: carry the coverage clients require and can issue a COI
workflow.gate: required coverage is in force and a COI can be issued

workflow.description: equip to a commercial standard within capital
workflow.gate: equipment meets the target contract at an affordable cost

workflow.description: work facility managers, brokers, bids and online channels
workflow.gate: at least two contract-finding channels are active
the business is an onboarded vendor with current documents

workflow.description: measure scope and price above fully-loaded cost
workflow.gate: every bid clears fully-loaded cost plus margin

workflow.action: deliver, invoice and fund the gap
workflow.description: meet the standard, invoice promptly and cover net-term cash
workflow.gate: the contract is delivered to standard and its cash gap is funded
the roadmap runs registration to first paid contract with dates and a fallback

workflow.description: renew licenses and insurance and refresh pricing
workflow.gate: renewal dates and reassessment triggers are tracked

priority_rationale: idea fit, demand and capital come first, then registration, licensing and insurance, then equipment and contract acquisition, then delivery, cashflow and scaling, with the synthesized roadmap and review last, so the business is legal and funded before it takes contracts.

dominance_rules.rule: never bid below fully-loaded cost to win a contract
dominance_rules.rationale: a money-losing contract is worse than no contract
dominance_rules.action: price to margin or walk away

dominance_rules.rule: obtain the required license or permit before performing regulated work
dominance_rules.rationale: unlicensed regulated work risks penalties and voided contracts
dominance_rules.action: license first, then perform the work

dominance_rules.rule: carry the insurance and bonds clients require before signing
dominance_rules.rationale: no commercial client signs without a valid COI and the business is exposed without it

dominance_rules.rule: classify every worker correctly under AB5 before paying them
dominance_rules.action: employ and insure correctly rather than pay 1099 cash

dominance_rules.rule: match the trade to available capital
dominance_rules.rationale: a high-capital trade with no funding stalls at launch
dominance_rules.action: start a trade the capital can actually equip

dominance_rules.rule: fund the net-term cashflow gap before committing to a contract
dominance_rules.rationale: insolvency from a payment gap ends the business
dominance_rules.trigger: taking a net-30 or net-60 contract
dominance_rules.action: secure reserves, deposits or financing first

dominance_rules.rule: protect current-contract quality before taking new work
dominance_rules.rationale: losing existing contracts to grow is negative-sum
dominance_rules.trigger: a new contract offer while capacity is tight
dominance_rules.action: stabilize and staff current work first

dominance_rules.rule: accept national-vendor subcontracts only when they clear cost with margin
dominance_rules.rationale: low-rate volume adds work without profit
dominance_rules.action: decline or renegotiate rates below cost

dominance_rules.rule: keep licenses, insurance and certifications current at all times
dominance_rules.rationale: a lapse suspends operations and vendor status

anti_rework_rules.rule: confirm license and permit needs before quoting regulated work
anti_rework_rules.prevents: quoting or doing work the business is not licensed to perform

anti_rework_rules.rule: confirm client insurance and COI requirements before bidding
anti_rework_rules.prevents: winning a bid the business cannot insure to sign

anti_rework_rules.rule: price to fully-loaded cost before submitting any bid
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an underbid contract that loses money over its term

anti_rework_rules.rule: verify cottage-food versus commercial-kitchen limits before baking to sell
anti_rework_rules.prevents: operating a food business outside its permitted scope

anti_rework_rules.rule: verify tow carrier permits and regulations before buying a tow truck
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a costly truck that cannot legally operate yet

anti_rework_rules.rule: classify labor correctly before hiring help
confirm client payment terms and fund the gap before committing capacity
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a cashflow crisis from net-term payment

anti_rework_rules.rule: match the trade to capital before buying equipment
anti_rework_rules.prevents: sinking capital into gear for a trade that cannot launch

iteration_protocol.trigger: a license, insurance or certification renewal nears
a bid is won or lost
iteration_protocol.action: refine the pricing model from the outcome

iteration_protocol.trigger: a roadmap milestone is hit or missed
